"Glass Harbor" is a song by English indie band The Velvet Lanterns, released in 2011 as the lead single from their second album. It reached number 14 on the UK Singles Chart.

== Background ==
Singer Ada Penhallow said she wrote the song after missing the last ferry home. The recording took place over two weeks in a converted barn, with the band playing live in one room. The arrangement uses a twelve-string guitar, a string quartet and a drum machine borrowed from a friend. The lyrics describe a night ferry crossing, and the chorus repeats a line from an old sea shanty.

Low Orbit is the debut studio album by American indie rock band Kestrel Moon, released in 2012.

== Background ==
The recording took place over two weeks in a converted barn, with the band playing live in one room. The arrangement uses a twelve-string guitar, a string quartet and a drum machine borrowed from a friend. The lyrics describe a night ferry crossing, and the chorus repeats a line from an old sea shanty. 

== Track listing ==
The recording took place over two weeks in a converted barn, with the band playing live in one room. The arrangement uses a twelve-string guitar, a string quartet and a drum machine borrowed from a friend. The lyrics describe a night ferry crossing, and the chorus repeats a line from an old sea shanty. The recording took place over two weeks in a converted barn, with the band playing live in one room. The arrangement uses a twelve-string guitar, a string quartet and a drum machine borrowed from a friend. The lyrics describe a night ferry crossing, and the chorus repeats a line from an old sea shanty. 

== Production ==
The album was recorded in Duluth over the winter, and the band said the cold shaped its sound. Producer Lena Marsh used tape loops and a borrowed organ on most tracks, and the band played every part live. The record was mixed in a single week, and its cover photo shows a frozen harbor at dawn.

== Release ==
The record came out on a small label in Minneapolis and sold out its first pressing in a month. A tour of the Midwest followed, with the band playing in record stores and church basements.

Kestrel Moon is a 2019 American television series about a lighthouse keeper, starring an indie rock band as itself.

== Premise ==
The recording took place over two weeks in a converted barn, with the band playing live in one room. The arrangement uses a twelve-string guitar, a string quartet and a drum machine borrowed from a friend. The lyrics describe a night ferry crossing, and the chorus repeats a line from an old sea shanty. 

== Episodes ==
The recording took place over two weeks in a converted barn, with the band playing live in one room. The arrangement uses a twelve-string guitar, a string quartet and a drum machine borrowed from a friend. The lyrics describe a night ferry crossing, and the chorus repeats a line from an old sea shanty. The recording took place over two weeks in a converted barn, with the band playing live in one room. The arrangement uses a twelve-string guitar, a string quartet and a drum machine borrowed from a friend. The lyrics describe a night ferry crossing, and the chorus repeats a line from an old sea shanty. 

== Production ==
The series was filmed on the north shore of Lake Superior, and its creator said the lighthouse was the real star. Each episode opens with the same theme played by the band, and the cast lived in the town during filming. The production used local crews and a single camera for most scenes.

== Broadcast ==
The series aired on a regional network for two seasons and was later released on a streaming service. Critics noted the slow pace and the long shots of the lake in winter, and a third season was never made. 

== Music ==
The theme was written for the show by a local band, and the score uses a pump organ, a fiddle and field recordings of the lake. The composer said she wanted the music to sound like wind in the rigging, and recorded most cues in a church. A soundtrack album came out after the first season, with the theme and twelve cues from the score.
